## Design

### 2026-10-25 – I first started by arranging all of the components I needed in a somewhat organized manner and just wired everything up. It was actually not too bad; the wiring took some research, but I would say it'

**7h**

I first started by arranging all of the components I needed in a somewhat organized manner and just wired everything up. It was actually not too bad; the wiring took some research, but I would say it's simpler than my week 1 PCB.
![schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/2968f6b08aecb7961f6c767c07eb9ec50d266183ab72c632f7bc5d8d72bef2b9.png)

I ran it through the Electrical Rules Checker, and to my horror, there were 20+ errors. But it turns out I just forgot to check off the ends where it's not connected to anything.
![ERC](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/1d84ab4588c8116b432bb79b508be488a435b697f54124806ac3ab74ab0bda7c.png)

Alongside fixing it, the lopsided diagram just wasn't sitting right with me, and I'm sort of a perfectionist, so I fixed it. I centered the keys, redid the wiring, and in the end I think it was worth it because it looks much nicer.
![CleanedUp](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/02b27c51bf9e4257cdafa6550a49aa2b4b37eeff9ea3e01e4dc543d115509d86.png)

I chose the footprints for each part I had in there and started on the PCB. The first thing I did was rearrange the keys and every component carefully, making sure everything was aligned because, once again, I'm a perfectionist.
![arranged](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/364633f3c6b1a36890432c3f44c015a7534e5210ba5df39cdc20cc30ba5348e6.png)

Then I wired everything up, trying to keep everything as uniform as possible. I think everything looks really nice.
![wiredpcb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/1ab8222da4ddd211de01a6cd1a8bab98f40527ade79d648021abfa3de5f08d86.png)

I had some leftover room on the left side, so I decided to add some art. I decided it would be the face of Nujabes and his album Luv Sic Hexalogy since I love both of them very much. (RIP).
![art](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/e4ee85ee09c810e1c656c0e7d8ba966dfd05305c6b6f5f69ac32eace0b3f3eb9.png)

With everything done on the PCB, this is what the final design looks like. I'm pretty proud.
![finalpcb](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/c3150ee960f8f249e48fdc0ec1e1b99bbf6b963c0355f9d34157bb6399ed1324.png)

### 2026-10-25 – The coding took even longer than designing the actual PCB, as I am pretty new to it and I decided to add a lot of features.

**8h**

The coding took even longer than designing the actual PCB, as I am pretty new to it and I decided to add a lot of features.

First, I imported all of the necessary things from the internet for MIDI stuff.
![import](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/bded24973468f9d4f33d5649f72c8c6171a52c1d3d53fc64e5eb172e6d9897b3.png)

This part tells the computer to treat the Raspberry Pi as a MIDI device.
![keysanddrums](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/ce5e67547724356289ec1550f2de863e12758fe56cbf2ba37f4685daae56ca83.png)

I added modes where you can switch between drums and notes. The initial setting starts as notes, and the base note is 48 or C3. The drums are channel 10 or 9 on the PCB since it starts at 0.

![initialnote](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/2930de2ae68d62891886d2cac65d5822d1e2adc0b16b53f55921dde5d7c9109f.png)

This is the code to switch the modes. It basically converts the signal from the switch on the PCB and translates that to either melody or drums based on the position.
![modeswitch](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/68e3822ec51f55a83c7af9929b3218277e959da72a66c28aeea8a37bbe3aa94a.png)

In a loop that repeats 100 times per second so there's no delay, it first checks for the mode. It takes the output and prints it.
![drumormelody](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/e90049943dd30596fec01a53c23d249e057344bb2c4ca18c19a14e5b87ac7eda.png)

This is a system to make sure that the notes don't go too high or too low. It checks the current number and whether it wants to go up or down. If it exceeds the limits, it doesn't do it.
![octaveboundary](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/0a7faf27d1adf79bc9a5207d624aea6b93b6d1d8998fb55e865c79356f6ee615.png)

This part checks if a key is pressed down or not, and if it is, it plays that note.
![playkey](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/638c2967d8f40409bbadb7a42bcbb49f668579ccfe45bb145fb7e02feeeb851c.png)

This is the volume slider, and I implemented a system where it takes in the movement, and if it's too small, it ignores it.
![volume](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/DRpFq7N3dxboV2y550rARcrYJQ0Bp1ow/83517a88c569c64f541178a9769ff00f83109366c7084e8b863598eefb995824.png)
